st: Rinse [[0.25 cup]] bulgur in a sieve, put it in a bowl, and cover with [[0.25 cup]] of the lemon juice. Let it soak for 20 minutes to soften.
Wash the parsley well and dry it completely in a salad spinner or with towels. Wet parsley turns the salad soggy.
Pick the leaves and chop them very finely with a sharp knife, along with the mint.
Dice the tomatoes and add them to the bulgur with the green onion.
Add the parsley and mint to the bowl.
Drizzle with the remaining lemon juice, [[0.33 cup]] olive oil, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper and toss gently.
Taste and adjust the lemon and salt. Serve right away with romaine leaves for scooping.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss the torn pita with [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and [[0.5 tbsp]] sumac, and spread on a baking sheet.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Cool.
Whisk [[0.25 cup]] lemon juice, [[0.25 cup]] olive oil, [[1 clove]] garlic, [[1 tbsp]] sumac, [[1 tbsp]] pomegranate molasses and [[0.75 tsp]] salt for the dressing.
Put the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers, radishes, green onion, mint and parsley in a large bowl.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss.
Add the pita chips just before serving so they stay crunchy.
Rinse [[1 cup]] bulgur, soak it in cold water for 10 minutes, then squeeze it very dry.
For the filling, cook [[0.5 lb]] ground lamb in [[1 tbsp]] olive oil for 6 minutes until browned and cooked through (160°F, 71°C).
Add the diced onion, pine nuts, [[0.5 tsp]] allspice, [[0.5 tsp]] cinnamon and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and cook 4 minutes. Cool.
In a food processor, blend the lean lamb, grated onion, bulgur, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] allspice into a smooth paste, adding a few ice cubes if it gets warm.
Wet your hands and take a golf-ball-size piece of the paste. Press a hole into it with your finger to make a thin shell.
Fill with about [[1 tbsp]] filling, close the opening, and shape into an oval with pointed ends.
Chill the shaped kibbeh for 20 minutes.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with yogurt or lemon.

ing: 15 oz each, drained, with liquid saved
st: Drain the chickpeas, saving the liquid. For extra smooth hummus, peel off the thin skins by hand.
Blend [[0.5 cup]] tahini and [[0.25 cup]] lemon juice in a food processor for 1 minute until pale and creamy.
Add [[2 cloves]] garlic, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] cumin and blend 30 seconds.
Add half the chickpeas and blend for 1 minute, then add the rest and blend for 3 minutes until very smooth.
With the machine running, add [[3 tbsp]] ice water, or chickpea liquid, until light and creamy.
Taste and add more salt or lemon.
Spread into a shallow bowl, making a well in the middle with a spoon.
Drizzle with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil and dust with [[0.25 tsp]] paprika. Serve with pita.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and line a baking sheet with foil.
Pierce the eggplants all over with a fork. Roast on the sheet for 40 minutes, turning once, until the skins blacken and collapse.
Cool for 10 minutes, then split open and scoop the soft flesh into a colander. Discard the skin.
Let the flesh drain for 5 minutes, pressing gently to remove excess liquid.
Chop the flesh roughly and put it in a bowl.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] tahini, [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice, [[2 cloves]] garlic, [[0.75 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] olive oil.
Taste and adjust the lemon and salt.
Spoon into a dish, drizzle with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil and top with parsley. Serve with pita.
Stir [[2.25 tsp]] yeast and [[1 tsp]] sugar into [[1.25 cups]] warm water and wait 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix in [[3.5 cups]] flour, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[2 tbsp]] olive oil. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C) with a baking sheet inside.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] za'atar with [[0.33 cup]] olive oil to make a spreadable paste.
Divide the dough into 6 balls, roll each to a 6-inch round, and press dimples with your fingertips.
Spread the za'atar paste on the rounds, leaving a border. Scatter the cheese on some if using.
Bake each on the hot sheet for 8 to 10 minutes until puffed with golden edges.
Serve warm, folded in half or with fresh vegetables.
Cut the chicken into 1.5-inch cubes.
Whisk [[0.5 cup]] yogurt, [[0.25 cup]] lemon juice, [[3 tbsp]] olive oil, [[5 cloves]] garlic, [[1 tbsp]] paprika, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Mix the chicken into the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers, leaving small gaps.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and oil the grates.
Cook the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until charred in spots and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest for 5 minutes. Serve with toum, pickles and pita.

ing: raw egg white, use pasteurized; optional
st: Peel the garlic and cut each clove in half. Remove any green sprouts, which taste bitter.
Process the garlic with [[1 tsp]] salt and the egg white in a food processor until finely minced, scraping the sides.
With the motor running, add [[1.5 cups]] oil in a very thin trickle, a few drops at a time at first.
After a few tablespoons of oil, add a little lemon juice so it keeps from splitting. Alternate oil and [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice in small amounts.
Keep going until fluffy, white, and thick like mayonnaise, about 8 minutes.
Beat in [[2 tbsp]] ice water to lighten the texture and mellow the garlic.
Scrape into a jar and refrigerate for up to 1 week. Because it contains raw egg white, use pasteurized eggs or omit it.
Put [[1 cup]] lentils and [[3 cups]] water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until almost tender.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add the onions with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Cook the onions for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown and a little crisp. Lower the heat if they scorch.
Take out half the onions and set them aside for topping.
Stir [[0.75 cup]] rice, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper into the lentils. Add the remaining onions and [[1 cup]] water.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve topped with the reserved onions and a drizzle of [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, with yogurt.
Make the syrup: boil [[1.5 cups]] sugar, [[1 cup]] water and [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice, then simmer 10 minutes. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] rose water and cool completely.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a 9 by 13 inch pan.
Mix the walnuts, pistachios, [[0.25 cup]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] cinnamon.
Lay 1 sheet of phyllo in the pan and brush with melted butter. Repeat for 10 sheets, keeping the rest covered with a damp towel.
Sprinkle with a third of the nut mix. Add 5 more buttered sheets, then more nuts, repeating until the nuts are used up.
Finish with 10 buttered sheets on top. Brush the top with butter.
Cut into diamonds or squares all the way down with a sharp knife.
Bake for 45 minutes until deep golden.
Pour the cool syrup over the hot baklava straight from the oven. Let it soak for at least 4 hours before serving.

ing: pitted dates mashed with 1 tbsp butter
st: Mix [[2 cups]] semolina and [[1 cup]] flour with [[0.25 cup]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] yeast. Pour in [[1 cup]] melted butter and rub until the mixture feels like wet sand.
Cover and rest the dough 1 hour, or overnight, so the semolina softens.
Add [[1 tbsp]] orange blossom water and enough warm milk, up to [[0.5 cup]], to make a soft dough that holds together.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Mix the date paste with chopped walnuts, if using, and roll into 16 small balls.
Take a golf-ball-size piece of dough, make a hollow, tuck in a date ball and seal. Press into a maamoul mold, or flatten and pattern with a fork.
Place on an ungreased sheet and bake 18 to 20 minutes until set and only lightly golden at the base.
Cool completely, then dust with [[2 tbsp]] powdered sugar. They are fragile while warm.
nt: Best swap: use dairy-free vegan butter 1:1 for the butter, and a fork or tongs for patterns if you have no maamoul mold.

st: Whisk the cornstarch with [[1 cup]] of the cold milk in a bowl until no lumps remain.
Heat the remaining milk and [[0.5 cup]] sugar in a medium pot over medium heat until steaming, stirring so it does not stick.
Pour in the cornstarch mixture while whisking. Cook 6 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from the heat and stir in [[1 tbsp]] orange blossom water and [[1 tsp]] rosewater.
Pour into 6 small bowls and cool 30 minutes at room temperature. Cover and chill at least 4 hours until firm.
Top with crushed pistachios and a drizzle of honey before serving.
nt: Thickened on the stovetop, then chilled
Best swap: almond milk and the same cornstarch for a dairy-free pudding.

st: Soak the raisins in a little warm water for 5 minutes until plump, then drain.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat until golden, about 3 minutes, shaking often. Cool on a plate.
In a pitcher, stir [[0.5 cup]] jallab syrup with [[4 cups]] cold water until fully mixed, then add [[1 tsp]] rose water.
Fill tall glasses with crushed ice and pour the jallab over.
Top with the raisins and pine nuts and serve with a spoon and straw.
nt: Don't cook: stir syrup into water, toast nuts only
Best swap: no jallab syrup, mix 6 tbsp pomegranate molasses with 2 tbsp date syrup or honey.

ing: Yukon Gold, cut in 1 inch cubes
st: Pat the potato cubes dry with a towel. Heat the vegetable oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat to about 350°F, so a cube sizzles right away.
Fry the potatoes in two batches for 8 to 10 minutes each, turning now and then, until deep golden and crisp outside and tender in the middle. Lift out onto paper towels.

In a clean skillet, warm [[1 tbsp]] olive oil over medium heat. Add [[3 clove]] minced garlic, the Aleppo pepper and the fried potatoes and toss for 1 minute until the garlic smells sweet but is not brown.
Off the heat, stir in the cilantro, lemon juice and salt. This is batata harra. Serve it warm.
Stir [[2 clove]] minced garlic, the dried mint and a pinch of salt into the labneh. Spread it in a shallow bowl, make a swirl with a spoon and pour [[2 tbsp]] olive oil over it.
Drain the olives and pickled turnips and arrange them in small bowls with the radishes.
Set the warm potatoes, labneh, olives, turnips and radishes on a big platter with the warm pita on the side. Eat by scooping with torn pita.
nt: Potatoes shallow-fried in oil, then tossed in a hot skillet with garlic; the rest is served cold
Best swap: strained thick Greek yogurt (drained 4 hours in a cheesecloth) for labneh, same amount.

st: Whisk the eggs in a large bowl with [[0.5 tsp]] salt, the pepper and allspice until smooth.
Stir in the parsley, mint and green onions, then sprinkle over [[2 tbsp]] flour and mix until just combined.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in about a quarter cup of batter per patty, making 3 or 4 at a time. Cook 3 minutes until the bottoms are golden and the edges are set.
Flip and cook another 2 minutes until fully cooked through to 160°F with no runny egg. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding oil as needed.
Serve warm or at room temperature with pita and yogurt.
nt: Best swap: bake it as one flat omelet in a greased 9 inch pan at 350°F for 20 minutes instead of frying.

st: Heat the oven to 325°F and line two trays with parchment.
Beat the ghee and powdered sugar for 5 minutes until white and creamy.
Mix in the vanilla and flour to form a soft dough. If it is sticky, chill for 15 minutes.
Roll into 1 inch balls and press into small rings or flat rounds.
Press one pistachio into the center of each cookie.
Bake for 14 minutes. They must stay pale, with no browning at all.
Cool on the tray; they are very delicate while warm.
nt: Best swap: use cold butter plus 1 tbsp oil for ghee, 1 to 1.

st: Stir the salt into the yogurt until evenly mixed.
Line a sieve with a clean cheesecloth or thin kitchen towel and set it over a deep bowl.
Pour in the yogurt, fold the cloth over the top and refrigerate for 8 hours. The longer it strains the firmer it gets.
Discard the whey that collected in the bowl. The labneh should be thick like cream cheese.
Spread on a plate with the back of a spoon, drizzle with [[3 tbsp]] olive oil and sprinkle with za'atar.
nt: Don't cook: salt and strain overnight
Best swap: strained coconut or soy yogurt for a dairy-free version, strained for 8 hours.

ing: for pink color, peeled and sliced
st: Wash all vegetables well. Cut cucumbers in half lengthwise if large, and cut the turnips, cauliflower and carrots into similar bite-sized pieces.
Stir [[3 tbsp]] salt into [[3 cups]] water until fully dissolved, then add [[1 cup]] white vinegar. This is your brine.
Pack the vegetables into a clean large jar, alternating colors, tucking in the garlic, chili, bay leaf and beet slices.
Pour the brine over until everything is covered by an inch. Weigh down with a small plate or a zip bag of brine so nothing floats.
Close loosely and keep at room temperature for 5 to 7 days. The brine will turn cloudy and pink and the vegetables will taste sour.
Refrigerate once the sourness is right. Serve with falafel, shawarma or grilled meats. Keeps for 1 month.
nt: Don't cook: brined and lightly fermented for 5 to 7 days
Best swap: skip the vinegar for a longer, fully fermented pickle; use 2 tbsp salt per 3 cups water.

st: Stir [[3 cup]] flour, [[2 tsp]] yeast, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[1 cup]] warm water and [[2 tbsp]] oil. Knead 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and rise 1 hour.
Toss spinach with [[1 tsp]] salt and let sit 10 minutes. Squeeze very dry.
Mix in the onion, sumac, lemon juice, pine nuts and [[2 tbsp]] oil.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Divide the dough into 12 balls and roll each into a 4 inch circle.
Put a heaping spoonful of filling in the center. Pinch the edges up into three corners to form a triangle, sealing all seams tightly.
Place on a lined tray and bake 15 to 18 minutes until golden. Serve warm or at room temperature.
nt: Best swap: use 2 tsp lemon zest plus extra lemon juice if you cannot find sumac; frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed, works 1 to 1.
